Larger end-to-end storage batches — 2026-10-19

Image: fuse-vault-large-batches-ram-debug.uf2
SHA-256: b83006b7dd2d3b3a7196902ebc29c60cfba2fec441d39edf050fb53d1b081e05
Source: d7c5206 plus local OTP routing, buffer and large-batch changes.
Build directory: build-board-large-batches, Release, FV_USB_IO_BYTES=65024.

This replaces the previous buffer-only experiment's 64+63-sector split.
The 127-sector USB request is now passed to the vault as ONE batch. The
authenticated storage layer writes its ciphertext as one SD operation and
its affected metadata as one operation, retaining existing publication/sync
ordering. Native SD permits 256 sectors, so it does not split this request.
The vault/storage maximum is 128 sectors (64 KiB); USB remains limited to
127 whole sectors (63.5 KiB) by its 16-bit transfer length.

The read path uses two 64-bit unset-sector mask words. The metadata cache
holds ten sectors, and its initialized-sector mask is now 16 bits. Existing
single-word authenticated-read callers retain the 64-sector API. Reads still
authenticate the whole batch before decryption; failed valid reads are wiped.
There is no new multi-sector atomicity guarantee and no disk-format change.

UI, physical TFT, USB storage and FIDO are enabled. RAM/debug screen and OTP
inspection are enabled; all other debug flags remain off, as in the baseline.
Flash via BOOTSEL after safely ejecting. Reconnect and unlock the existing
vault; do not perform fresh setup. Existing data/passkeys remain compatible.

Expected fixed RAM: 434.1 KiB, 6 KiB above the buffer-only experiment due to
expanded metadata caches. At the previous 14.9 KiB heap reservation, about
71 KiB remains uncommitted. Hardware stack usage is not measured by this.

Repeat the same file, cipher stack, connector and viewer workload. Compare
the steady device upload rate and elapsed time through the final flush.
Safely eject/reconnect and verify the copy. Retest FIDO during transfer.
Actual speed improvement still needs measurement on hardware.

Validation:
- Full 45/45 host/FIDO tests passed with assertions, ASan and UBSan.
  ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0; no leak-check claim.
- Full physical-UI/MSC/FIDO firmware build passed; UF2 identity checked.
- Large-batch tests cover 127/128 sectors, mixed unset/written sectors across
  bit 63/64, all ten metadata-cache entries, upper-half corruption and whole
  output wiping, reopen/decrypt, bounds, and interrupted bitmap publication.
- SD mock counters confirm a 128-sector data operation; USB worker test
  confirms its 127-sector request is passed through without splitting.
- Actual TinyUSB BOT tests passed with 4/16/32/63.5 KiB buffers under ASan/UBSan.

Rollback builds in this directory:
fuse-vault-buffer-635k-ram-debug.uf2 (large buffers, split vault operations)
fuse-vault-d7c5206-ram-debug.uf2 (original 32 KiB buffers and batches)
